A.explanation: All colours travel at the same speed $c$ in vacuum, so with equal distance the travel time $t = s/c$ is identical.

B.explanation: Blue does not travel faster in vacuum - dispersion with blue fastest applies in glass, not in vacuum.

C.explanation: Red does not have a higher vacuum speed despite its lower frequency and longer wavelength.

D.explanation: The wavelength order red-green-blue does not give a speed order in vacuum where all have speed $c$.

hints: Notice the question states the pulses travel in a vacuum for the full Sun to Mars distance, with the same starting time and same distance.
Recall that red, green and blue light are all electromagnetic waves with different frequency but the same vacuum speed $c \approx 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Connect equal speed and equal distance to travel time using $t = s/v$ to compare the arrival times of the three pulses.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: three brief pulses of red, green and blue light start at the same time, travel the same distance from the Sun to Mars, entirely in vacuum.
State the governing rule: all electromagnetic waves, whatever their colour, frequency or wavelength, travel at the same speed in vacuum, $c \approx 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Set up the travel time for each pulse as $t = s/v$, where $s$ is the Sun to Mars distance and $v$ is the wave speed.
Substitute $v = c$ for each colour, so $t_{red} = s/c$, $t_{green} = s/c$ and $t_{blue} = s/c$ with the same $s$ and same $c$.
Conclude the times are equal, so no colour pulls ahead and they reach Mars together. This is option A.
